steps.text: Who are you...?
Where did you come from?
You came from nowhere, have no kin, and don't even know who you are...
Could it be that you're a Xian, like in the stories?
Jingzhe, when insects wake.
The weather finally clears up after a few days of early spring rain.
A square platform sits in the center of the public square—it resembles both a stage and altar with a statue silently standing on top.
It is a sculpture of a simply dressed woman with facial features hard to perceive, but one can easily tell where her gaze is looking.
A boy carefully offers a verdant seedling to the statue with a deferential bow.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Shennong, bless us...

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Everything has to go smoothly this year...

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Laoshi?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: I was looking for you and the soil samples I asked for—what are you doing here?
The boy turns sideways, trying to obstruct his 'offering' from the other's view.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: We'll be transplanting the seedlings in two days, and this year is the first I'm taking charge of an experimental field. I'm really worried that something might go wrong, or I'll do a bad job...

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I've heard from my qianbeis at the Bureau they always come here to pay their respects in moments like these... I'm pretty new, so maybe Shennong will be kinder to me.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: What have those elders been teaching you youths...?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Will you stop farming if something does happen?
The mute statue is covered in mud from the past few days of wind and rain, as if it has just returned from a day of work in the fields.
The woman steps forward and gently wipes the mud off the statue.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: 'Shennong' spent her whole life diligently working the fields, but ended up worshiped as a Xian by you lot, expecting her to solve your problems.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: They only come to visit her when they have problems they can't solve, or obstacles they can't overcome.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Was 'Shennong' a real person?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Why do you ask?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: She came up with a calendar system and figured the twenty-four solar terms a thousand years ago... she even managed to cultivate such a wide expanse of farmland in a place so perilous...

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I honestly can't imagine that being the work of a single woman.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: It doesn't matter if you believe it or not—the changes in the seasons and soil beneath our feet are real and true.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Someone must have done these things in the first place, for stories to be passed down about them.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: What kind of woman was she to achieve such feats?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Her, huh...? Just an inconsiderate fool, that's all.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: What does this continent look like from above?

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: You told me your body was once taller than a mountain, and the clouds floating in the sky did not even clear your shoulders—what was the view like up there?

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: The endless stretch of mounts you see are undulating slopes of earth to me; what you take for towering trees are more or less the seedlings growing by the roadside here.
Dead mounts and still water for a myriad years.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: So you couldn't see the flowers and trees clearly, nor make out the cries of the fowlbeasts?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: That sounds like a lonely life...

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: You don't fear me?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Why would I? You don't look like a monster, you look like us.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: But we're not the same at all. My lifespan is thousands of times longer than yours, and I could easily reduce you to dust, were you to anger me.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Pfft—

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: You dare laugh...?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: I've heard tall tales like that before. The Xians in these stories always descend to the mortal realm on account of boredom and loneliness.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Why turn yourself into a mortal and come to our realm otherwise? Sure, turn me into dust, but then who are you gonna talk to?

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: I'm not—

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: *sigh* Why the violent threats when you've got such power?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: If I had a body as big as you did, I'd let people plant crops of all kinds on me! Hey, how about that? Can you make plants grow better too?

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: That'd be easy. I'll even prove it right now... see?
The girl gently waves her hand, and in the next instant, a green sorghum seedling in the ground ripens, bearing a bountiful harvest of grain.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: I could turn this entire snowfield into farmland, if I wanted to.
The farmer's eyes grow wide, and she does not speak for quite a while.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Does it tire you out, doing that?

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: Doesn't take much effort. Much less than your slow farming techniques.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Then, what do you want from us in return?

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: What could I even want from you lot? I just did that on a whim, since I'm in a good mood.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Then...

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: No, no... it's better if you don't do it again.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: I can't only think about now. You helped us today, but what if your mood turns sour? You might just leave us.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: If we were to depend on you, then wouldn't the crops here vanish once you left? We'd have forgotten how to grow our own food and we'd end up hungry.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: So it's best we work hard on our own to cultivate the land, and we'll free ourselves from those anxieties too.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: I've met many others who witnessed a shred of my power and immediately started begging me to grant them more.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: But you. How much land could you cultivate, even if you were to till the fields until you died?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: However much I can, I just have to try my best. I'm sure someone will continue what I started after I'm gone.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: That doesn't make sense though? You said you 'can't only think about now', but you changed your tune to 'I just have to try my best'?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Makes sense to me. We mortals can't turn our wishes real like a Xian can. We push ourselves and live with some aspirations unrealized. That's normal, and it keeps us grounded...

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: Keeps you grounded?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Hmm... here.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: What's this about?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: I can't learn your supernatural farming techniques, but I can teach you how we mortals do it. It's a bit slow, but it works.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Learn how we farm, and you might just understand how us mortals think and feel too.
Is it tough, being human?

a.text: Of course! Just look at the frostbite on my hands... I'm still young, but my back already aches on rainy days.

steps.text: I could take you somewhere else, a place with picturesque views and spring-like weather all year round. You wouldn't have to labor like this, and there's so much food over there you couldn't finish it all even if you were to live ten times as long.

a.text: Haha, I knew it! You're afraid to be alone. You just want some company, right?

steps.text: You don't believe me?

a.text: Of course I believe you. This great land is so vast I'm sure a place as good as that exists somewhere... but I'm also afraid. Afraid that I'll never want to come back after visiting your utopia.
Our mortal lives are too short. As long as I can grow these crops right here, I'll be satisfied.
Although, going out to have fun with you isn't entirely off the table, if...
Only if you promise me everyone in this world will never go hungry again.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Hmmhmm...♪

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: You're in a good mood?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Look, the seeds I tried planting here have sprouted. Now we have another crop to feed ourselves with.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Give it a few more years, and we'll manage to turn this patch of barren land into fertile fields and grow enough food to sustain several more villages.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: Those villages—you know the people there?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: No... not at all.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: Then why do you care about them?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Well... isn't it normal to worry about others? To help each other out?

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: You keep yourself alive just on your own, what have they helped you with?

spans.text: You keep yourself alive just on your own, what have

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Maybe they can't help me now, but in the future they might...

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: So you give them food now, in exchange for a possible future payoff?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: You can't really put it that way either... Oh! I almost got lost in your questions.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: You've lost me too.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: I remember a phrase from a book written by the sages—'All men are kin, as with living things'—it roughly means that we should care for everyone and everything, like the plants and trees.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: I'm bad with words, I can't explain it well. I just think the plants and trees right here are pretty and want to grow more of them; I don't like how hunger feels, and I don't want anyone else to suffer it either.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: *sigh*... A Xian like you couldn't know what starvation feels like, how unbearable it gets...

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: So what's it like?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Your stomach hurts, your organs feel like someone's twisting them. Your body loses all its strength, and you just feel empty and nonexistent.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: As if your body's experiencing every suffering on this land at the same time.

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: And how does that feel?

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Like... when a most beloved relative, or best friend passes away, and you know they'll never come back...

steps.name: Ignorant Girl
steps.text: I still don't understand...

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: You say you don't, but you've been here with me for so long.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Well, I do enjoy our days together. My work feels less tough when I have someone to chat with.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: It'll be hard for me if you leave one day, so I'll figure out a way to make you stay here for a while longer.

steps.name: Rustic Farmer
steps.text: Oh, I didn't mean you have to stay here... I just remembered that you said you wanted to understand us 'mortals'.

spans.text: to stay here... I just remembered that you said you wanted to understand us 'mortals'.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: You called 'Shennong' a fool...

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Have you heard the old farmers saying you can't look up when harvesting?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: You have to keep your head down, and courageously reap the crops before you. Once you look up and look out at the fields that stretch to no end, you won't be able to move.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Humans live only a few short decades, and lack the luxury of time to care about what will come after they're gone. Focusing on what's in front of you is tiring enough.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: But once you lock in on something, you'll achieve many things before you even realize it.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Can you guess how far Dahuang's fields stretched when Shennong passed?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Maybe half of what we have right now? Or one-third?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: See that hillside to the south? Back then, the fields stretched to the foot of that mountain.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: That small...?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: The conditions then were incomparably worse than what we have right now. We didn't have these Originium devices, and it took so much effort just to pull a proper plow through the fields.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: We couldn't dig up the rocks on the mountains, nor the permafrost up north. So Dahuang stretched only from that hillside in the south to the Shennong statue right here.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Where was this recorded? How do you remember it so clearly?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Where exactly...? I've forgotten myself.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: The books say Shennong wanted to cultivate the land up north in her later years, but eventually succumbed to illness on her northward search for the 'Shen Gu' super grain.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: So why does this statue face southward?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Shennong labored her entire life away just to prevent her fellow man from going hungry and cold. She would've been very attached to the people of her hometown.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: That's probably where she was looking, in her final moments.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Actually, what made you decide to become an Nongye Tianshi in the first place?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: When I was young, I learned how it felt to starve, once. Since then, I decided I wouldn't let anyone else go through that.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: So you also suffered a famine...

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Well... that was long, long ago.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: Just like Shennong...

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Dahuang has many farmers and Nongye Tianshis that have more or less have similar reasons as to why they're here.
The sun gradually rises as the spring breeze blows warmth into the air and onto the people.
The wind pushes the clouds away, letting a slanted ray of sunlight shine onto the statue's face.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I'm suddenly thinking about the various legends we have here, 'Shennong', 'Excavator', 'Yan'...

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: We still don't know if they were historical people or just myths. Could it be that Shennong wasn't just one woman?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: She only hoped for more to follow in her footsteps, instead of remembering who she was, so she hid her identity.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: But this way, no one really remembers the person she was...

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: If someone like that really existed, do you think she'd care if the people here remembered her name at all, if she could see what Dahuang has become?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Or maybe she was just shy and didn't want to leave her name and likeness behind.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: If you don't behave and go back home, there won't be any meat in your meals for the next few days.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Shu... you shouldn't be bullying the elderly.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Then act your age. Do you think it's romantic to watch the snow fall outside with just one layer on you? Today is Xiaohan, you know.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I knew it. My waist always starts hurting this time of year, right on schedule... how could you expect me to just lie in bed at home?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: This winter has been so cold. Will the soil manage to defrost in time for the next spring...?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: That's not something you should be worrying about right now. Keep neglecting your health and you'll might not even make it to next spring.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: That won't do... I'm planning to go north again when spring comes. I got lost in the northeastern forests last time, so I'll try walking west this time.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: You're trying to anger me.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Once you're in the ground, I'll have them build a statue here, looking towards the north that's always on your mind.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I couldn't ask for anything more.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: But don't let them carve the statue the way I am now. Too ugly.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: And as for the clothes, reference the outfit your brother gave me. I'm quite fond of it.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Oh, speaking of which... I haven't seen him in so many years. I wonder if I'll manage to see him one more time...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Time flies so fast... it feels like I met you just yesterday. Several decades gone, just like that.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Over the course of those decades, Dahuang's fields have tripled in size, and our annual crop yields have more than doubled... everyone calls you Shennong, the godly farmer, why not be content with that?

spans.text: Over the course of those decades, Dahuang's fields have tripled in size, and our annual crop yields have more than doubled... everyone calls you
the godly farmer, why not be content with that?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Humans are always greedy for more. We're never content.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Grow two yields of rice this year, and you'll want three the next; once you have a hundred mu of fields, you'll want two hundred...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Someday, when Dahuang's fields stretch beyond what I can see from here, I wonder if I'll still be able to visit the picturesque place you talked about?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Sure. Once you're well again, I'll bring you there in the spring.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: You're lying to me again... I realized it a long time ago, you blink hard whenever you lie.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Shu... you knew this day would come.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Of course. Didn't I say so? I was used to this long before even I met you.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: All living things abide the laws of mortality...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Do you feel it now?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Feel what?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Feel like a human...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Feel happiness over something trivial, feel sad knowing how something ends, feel anticipation, reluctance...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I know how you feel... this is how humans connect with one another, through our common feelings.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: You spent your entire life just to teach me a single thing... you're a pretty bad teacher, honestly.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: So can you stay here in my stead, after I'm gone?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I don't need you to be their patron saint. Just live here, as a human.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Teach the children the farming methods we developed, a woman as bright as you will surely do a better job teaching than me.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: They'll remember there was once a woman who spent her entire life on this freezing snowfield just so her people wouldn't go hungry.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Just me alone? I clearly had a Xian in human form at my side this whole time.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: But no matter. You live the same way as we do, so no one knows you're a runaway Xian who sneaked into the mortal realm.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I won't get to see it, but perhaps a day will come when Dahuang becomes the place you spoke of... I'm sure there'll be many by your side to admire the scenery, and you won't be lonely anymore.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: When the winter jasmines on that hillside bloom next year, will you weave a wreath of them for me?

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: It's getting late, Laoshi. I'll go prepare the transplanting tools.

steps.name: He Sheng
steps.text: I'll give it my all, no matter how this year goes.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Mm, off you go.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: See? They still remember you.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: An ascetic like you is still on their minds, even after a thousand years... What can I say?
A fowlbeast brings up a small yellow flower in its beak and drops it on the statue's bamboo hat.
It seems to have picked a good nesting spot, and fetches several more flowers with branches in bunches. Yellow flowers soon cover the brim of the hat.
The flowers bloom so beautifully after that parting, I wonder if you still know the way home.
